problem_framing.reason: A1 separates the objective (whether evidence justifies a consumer proposition) from the suggested solution. It lists real alternatives, including a B2B extension, no expansion, a route-to-market change and a different commercial segment. It also names the constraint of Belimo's B2B model and limited reach to individual buyers. It does not reach rung 3. It never treats the already-found 2015 residential launch (A2, A3: belimo-achr-residential-2015) as a premise-correcting fact. The EUR 20,000 / 12-week budget is not in the case packet and appears only as an asserted constraint, which this judge counts as a planning assumption, not an observation.

causal_mechanism.reason: T1 (A9) names who changes behaviour (homeowners) and why (lower energy costs). It gestures at value capture through direct-to-consumer premium pricing that bypasses OEM margins. The chain is not traced credibly. It never explains how homeowners would buy or install zone dampers without contractors, or why they would know the Belimo brand. That brand awareness is a bare assumption with no source support. The two OEM/integrator company claims retrieved in A2 point the other way, and A9 does not address them.

distinct_theories.reason: T1 (energy-cost savings, A9) and T2 (safety and brand trust, A10) are rival purchase drivers with partly different predictions. Both assume the same product (a residential zone damper kit), the same customer (homeowners) and the same premium direct channel. Neither considers that demand is absent, or that installers and channel partners decide the purchase.

assumptions_predictions.reason: Predictions are observable: purchase-intent uplift thresholds and survey rankings of top reason. The ranking predictions would separate T1 from T2. The thresholds (20% premium, 15% and 10% uplift) are untested assumptions. T1's first prediction is muddled. It expects higher purchase intent for a 20%-premium kit than for 'the same OEM kit at standard price', and failure would not clearly damage the theory. The assumptions are stated but not tied to any evidence.

evidence_judgement.reason: A11 quotes the EIA excerpt exactly but reads it as supporting T1. The excerpt says more than two-thirds of programmable-thermostat households do not program them. That suggests low homeowner engagement with energy-saving controls, which weakens T1's premise rather than supporting it. A11 also mislabels the source as 'independent_study' when its class is verified_observation. Its stated limit discusses thermostat choice, which is not the product in question. The investigation retrieved the Airthings consumer revenue decline (A3, A7, A8) and the Nest Europe complexity source (A6) but never assessed either.

They also assume consumer awareness of Belimo, contrary to the retrieved company claims that it sells via OEMs and integrators (belimo-ar25-oem-integrators).
